feedback: [check 5] Legibility: At 1440px, <div.hero-inner > h1.phrase > span.word> "thousands" at 158px over section.hero (background-image): #f0391e is under 3:1 across 100% of one pixel row through its glyphs (2.27:1 on #524742). Give the text a flat ground that clears the ratio (a background on its own box), or stop the lines, image or layer behind it short of the text.

1. (Judgment 6, SHELL `ground_material: grain` / `ground_strategy: dark-void`) At 1440 and in fold 1 at 360, the hero field reads as a flat, muddy grey-brown box (roughly #45403E) with a soft blur, not a warm near-black void (#160C0A) carrying grain. No grain is visible, and the haze washes out the ground. Bring the hero field back to the warm-black page ground, add a fine visible grain, and keep the vermilion glow as a contained lamp in the void rather than a grey wash over the whole field. That restores the brief's "lamp over a table at dusk", with "thousands" glowing out of darkness.

1. (Judgment 6, `ground_strategy: dark-void` / `ground_material: grain`) The hero field renders as a flat mid grey-brown (roughly #4A403E) at 1440 and at 360, not warm-black #160C0A with grain. It reads as a grey box, the failure SHELL forbids. Put the hero field on the #160C0A void with a fine, visible warm grain so the vermilion word glows out of darkness as declared.

2. (Judgment 6, ground) There is a hard near-black rectangle behind "thousands" that nothing declares. At 1440 it runs about 290px past the end of the word, to x≈969, so it reads as a misapplied background rather than a design choice. The same slab appears at 360. Remove it so the word sits directly on the void. If the slab is where the dark-void ground ended up, move that ground to the whole hero field instead.

1. Judgment 3 (Type Treatment `texture: vertical`): The hero "thousands" and its deck are set entirely horizontally on a plain field at both 1440 and 360. Nothing in the hero carries the declared vertical texture. The only vertical element is the rail nav stack, which is navigation, not hero treatment. Execute `texture: vertical` in the hero itself, for example as a vertical setting or vertical type texture tied to the word. Keep the read of "thousands" → deck clear of it.
